data.name: Tarsus
data.gender_notes: Tarsus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Tarsus has Greek origins and is derived from the name of the ancient city in Cilicia, which was considered the home of several early Christian saints. The name is believed to mean 'City of Taurus' and may be associated with the strength and power of the bull, which was a common symbol in ancient Greek mythology.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Christian tradition, the name Tarsus symbolizes strength, courage, and resilience, reflecting the spiritual qualities of the early Christian saints associated with the city.
data.etymology: Tarsus belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “City of Taurus.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tarsus total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: טרסוס
in_hebrew.meaning: עיר בדרום אנטוליה, מרכז סחר חשוב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם טרסוס מקורו בשפה היוונית ומשמעותו עיר בדרום אנטוליה, מרכז סחר חשוב. בעברית, השם טרסוס קשור לעיר טרסוס באנטוליה, שהייתה מרכז סחר חשוב בתקופה הרומית והביזנטית. השם טרסוס נזכר גם בברית החדשה, כמקום הולדתו של שאול איש טרסוס, הידוע יותר בשם פאולוס.

in_greek.name: Ταρσός
in_greek.meaning: πόλις ἐν Κιλικίᾳ, σπουδαῖος ἐμπορικός σταθμός
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Ταρσός προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἀρχαία Κιλικιανή λέξη καὶ σημαίνει πόλις ἐν Κιλικίᾳ, σπουδαῖος ἐμπορικός σταθμός. Ἡ Ταρσὸς ἦταν σημαντικὸ ἐμπορικό κέντρο στὴν Κιλικία τῆς Μικρᾶς Ἀσίας καὶ ἡ γενέτειρα τοῦ Σαύλου, τοῦ γνωστοῦ ὡς Παύλου.

in_latin.name: Tarsus
in_latin.meaning: city in Cilicia, important trade center
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Tarsus is derived from the Greek and Latin words for city in Cilicia, an important trade center. In the Roman and Byzantine periods, Tarsus was a significant commercial hub. The name Tarsus is also associated with Saint Paul, who was born in Tarsus, Cilicia.

in_english.name: Tarsus
in_english.meaning: a city in ancient Cilicia, modern-day Turkey
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tarsus originates from ancient Greek and Latin roots, signifying a city in Cilicia, a region in modern-day Turkey. Historically, Tarsus was an important commercial center and the birthplace of Saint Paul, also known as Paul of Tarsus. The name Tarsus symbolizes cultural richness, spiritual significance, and a strong historical heritage in Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: Today, Tarsus is recognized as an important site in Christian history, having played host to several early apostles and martyrs. The city is believed to be the birthplace of the apostle Paul, who is considered one of the most influential figures in Christian tradition. Tarsus has also been a cultural melting pot throughout history, with influences from Greek, Roman, Byzantine, and Ottoman empires shaping its architecture, art, and traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, Tarsus holds great spiritual significance as the birthplace and home of several saints, including Paul and the martyrs Lycia and Evagrius. It is a pilgrimage site for many Christians who seek to connect with the spiritual legacy of these early saints. Additionally, the city's association with the bull may symbolize the strength and power of God, as well as His guidance and protection over His people. Tarsus serves as a reminder of the rich history and spiritual depth of the Christian faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Tarsus is a symbol of strength and resilience in faith. This name derives from the ancient city in Anatolia, known for its sturdy structures and tenacious inhabitants. In the Christian context, Tarsus represents the unwavering commitment to follow Christ, even amidst trials and challenges.

biblical_reference.note: Tarsus is mentioned in the New Testament as the birthplace of Paul of Tarsus.

historical_references.reference: Tarsus is believed to have been the birthplace of the Apostle Paul (Saul of Tarsus), who was a key figure in the early Christian movement.
historical_references.context: Tarsus was an important city in the Roman province of Cilicia, located in modern-day Turkey.

historical_references.reference: The early Christian community in Tarsus is mentioned in Acts 9:31 when it is stated that the disciples in Judea heard that ‘God was also working through the grace given to the apostles in Syria and Cilicia.’
historical_references.context: This suggests that Christianity had a presence in Tarsus early on in the faith's history.

modern_usage.modern_context: Tarsus is an ancient city located in southeastern Turkey, renowned for its historical significance and rich cultural heritage. It is most famously associated with the New Testament and the birthplace of the Apostle Paul. Today, Tarsus is home to the University of Tarsus, a significant educational institution that attracts students from around the world. Tarsus can be explored through various platforms including Google Maps, which offers satellite and street view imagery, Wikipedia, which provides extensive historical and cultural information, and the Turkish Tourism Agency, which offers guided tours and travel packages to experience the city's unique attractions.
